analysis.title: Americas Energy: Oil & Gas - E&P: Oil E&Ps Well Positioned Even At Long-Term $70-$75/bbl WTI; Highlight Buys on PR, DVN and OXY (on Conviction List)
key_insights: Energy outperformed ahead of 3Q26 earnings: XLE +11% vs S&P 500 -1% over the past month, with geopolitical tensions, elevated commodity prices and November election uncertainty cited as drivers.
GS oil E&P stocks rose +14% in the past month as the 2027/2028 WTI curve re-rated +11%/+8%. GS still sees room to run.
GS anchors oil E&P valuation to a $73/bbl mid-cycle WTI price and sees a 12% average FCF yield on 2027/2028 for oily E&P coverage.

At current strip WTI ($81/bbl in Exhibit 1), the average 2027/2028 FCF yield for oily E&P coverage is 16% (15.6% in the exhibit). GS sees material upside risk to medium-term FCF given the risk premium in the forward curve.
OXY: Buy, price target raised to $76 (18% upside) from $69. GS sees a long-term cash flow improvement pathway but notes near-term GOA operational headwinds that materialized at the end of 3Q26.

OXY has retired $8.6 bn of debt year-to-date as of 2Q26 earnings. GS sees line of sight to the $10.0 bn principal debt milestone in 4Q26 and wants clarity on debt reduction goals beyond that. OXY raised its base dividend 8% and resumed buybacks in 1H26.

OXY has underperformed large-cap E&P peers over the past 3 months (+11% vs +13% average for COP, FANG, EOG, DVN). GS seeks clarity on the cash flow improvement plan and capital allocation at 3Q26 earnings.

PR: Buy reiterated, price target raised to $29 (14% upside). Drivers are economic oil production growth, accretive ground-game transactions and a natural gas realization inflection as Waha pricing improves.

PR raised FY2026 oil production guidance to 199 Mbo/d at the midpoint (+10% y/y) while midpoint cash capex stays about 1% below 2025. Average working interest rose to above 80% for FY2026 from 75-80% as of 1Q26.
PR is up 74% year-to-date vs 51% for XLE and 48% for oily peers. GS still sees upside, with PR at a 14% average 2027/2028 FCF yield vs 12% for oily peers (EOG, FANG, DVN, OVV).
DVN: Buy, price target raised to $59 (15% upside) from $55. DVN trades at a 14% average 2027/2028 FCF yield, a discount to large-cap peers.

DVN lagged large-cap oil E&P peers over the past month (7% vs 14% average) on uncertainty over its portfolio review. It announced a $4.2 bn sale of its Eagle Ford exit to Crescent Energy, expected to close around YE2026.
GS raised its DVN 3Q26 expected FCF to $1.95 bn (+27% vs prior). Items to watch at earnings: 2027 capital plans, use of Eagle Ford proceeds, and progress toward $1.0 bn of merger synergies by YE2027.
GS raised 4Q26 oil estimates to $100/bbl Brent from $90/bbl and keeps mid-cycle Brent of $80/$75 for 2027/2028 and Henry Hub of $3.50/$3.50 per MMBtu.
GS cut target FCF yields by 1.0% for OXY, APA, FANG, DVN, PR and OVV, and by 0.5% for EOG and MGY, citing the risk premium in the forward curve. It raised the TALO target yield by 1.5%.

MUR valuation methodology changed to a blend of 50% FCF yield and 50% DCF. The target FCF yield was cut to 6.0% from 12.0% on high capital intensity from the Bubale appraisal program and exploration. The price target rose to $44 from $36.
Other target changes: FANG to $235 from $215, VNOM to $54 from $53, TALO to $22 from $20, EOG to $158 from $148, OVV to $72 from $65, APA to $47 from $44, MGY to $26 from $27.
Ratings: Sell on APA (-9% downside), CRK, TOU-CA. Neutral on MUR, MGY, EOG, RRC. Buy on OXY, TALO, FANG, VNOM, DVN, PR, OVV, EXE, EQT, AR.

sector_views.rationale: Oil E&Ps look well positioned even at a long-term $70-$75/bbl WTI. 12% average FCF yield on 2027/2028 at the $73 mid-cycle price and 16% at the current strip.
Mixed ratings: Buys on EXE, EQT and AR, Sells on CRK and TOU-CA, Neutral on RRC. Gas E&P average upside is 2% vs 8% for oil E&Ps.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 earnings previews: GS expects solid operational performance for DVN, with 3Q26 expected FCF raised to $1.95 bn (GS estimate, +27% vs prior GS estimate).

GS raised 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA estimates (GS estimates, new vs old): TALO $341 mn vs $276 mn (+24%), OVV $1,319 mn vs $1,163 mn (+13%), APA $1,744 mn vs $1,638 mn (+6%), MUR $531 mn vs $502 mn (+6%), MGY $336 mn vs $316 mn (+6%), VNOM +4%, DVN $3,749 mn vs $3,647 mn (+3%), OXY $4,187 mn vs $4,101 mn (+2%), FANG +2%, PR +2%. EOG was cut 3% to $4,476 mn from $4,596 mn.
OXY 3Q26: GS flags near-term headwinds in GOA operations that materialized at the end of 3Q26, and looks for commentary on capital allocation and the cash flow improvement plan.
PR: FY2026 oil production guidance of 199 Mbo/d at the midpoint (+10% y/y), as raised during the 2Q26 earnings report.
DVN 3Q26: GS looks for updates on the portfolio review, 2027 capital and activity plans, use of Eagle Ford sale proceeds and progress on $1.0 bn merger synergies by YE2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS values oil E&Ps at this mid-cycle WTI price.
The current strip sits well above the mid-cycle anchor, lifting 2027/28 FCF yields from 12% to 16%.
The forward curve re-rated higher, which supports E&P cash flow estimates.
Gas price deck used for valuation.

charts_described: Exhibit 1: 2027/28 FCF yield at GS mid-cycle ($73/bbl) vs strip WTI ($81/bbl). The average rises from 12.1% to 15.6%, with TALO highest at 23.8% on strip and MUR lowest at 10.4%.
Exhibit 3 plots OXY net debt, preferred equity and WTI price, and GS estimates OXY reaching below the $10 bn principal debt target in 4Q26.
Exhibit 4: PR natural gas sales net of processing costs and post-hedge realizations as a share of Henry Hub, with GS expecting a tighter Waha environment in 2027/2028 to help PR.
Exhibit 5: DVN 14% average 2027/2028 GS FCF yield compared with FANG, OXY, EOG and COP and the peer average.
